verification.per_request_verification_boundary: The target report printed four accepted same-thread home comparisons. The terminal aggregates allow contract/hash/checksum comparison but cannot independently recheck every per-request schedule, checksum and status from raw CSVs.

statistical_boundaries: Source SHA256 covers original file bytes including CRLF; values are printed precision, not a reconstruction of unprinted raw records.
Six configurations have one run each at seed421. The 1536-request cohort has nominal top 1% of 15.36 requests but not guaranteed independent tail samples or a valid effect confidence interval.

Latency cohort uses planned arrivals [2,18); whole execution CPU includes warmup/drain and is divided by 1920 completed requests. This CPU window excludes Driver/pool/trace-buffer construction and post-run CSV writing.
Driver whole-run mean/p99 and formal cohort mean/p99 have different populations and are stored separately.

Flow means can be added at their precision; separate planned-latency, attempt-lag and attempt-to-finish p99 values cannot be subtracted into a decomposition. Attempt timestamps precede request construction/root add and are not Folly enqueue timestamps.

Matched report deltas were computed before decimal formatting. Original printed deltas and deltas derived from rounded rows are preserved separately; an observed 0.001ms difference is a rounding distinction.

Matched latency deltas are differences of cohort statistics, not quantiles of per-request differences. Derived percentages and CPU deltas are labelled separately from printed matched output. Every included policy comparison uses the same thread budget; no across-thread pooling.

The 96 one-second rows count scheduled arrivals, attempts and completions in wall-time bins. Completion totals may be 1537 while the planned cohort remains 1536 because entering/leaving backlog differs; all boundary accounting is conserved.

Request backlog includes generator lag and is not Folly queue depth. Boundary values 0/1 and peak-inflight=3 show observed overlap without proving steady state, continuous saturation, all-pool competition or absence of within-bin queueing.

Home attempt-lag p99 is elevated compared with candidate runs; no mechanism cause can be identified from these request-only records. Do not attribute lag exclusively to kernel scheduling, L2 or CPU binding.

Trace0 cannot recover Q/I/O, callback occupancy, first-fork timing, migration counts or operator CPU/wall. Missing observations are not zero, and historical trace1 figures cannot be inserted as this batch measurements.

The CPU sets/nominal capacities are identical across thread budgets, but worker budgets differ. Each target pool still corresponds to one selected hardware cluster; historical four-pool behavior does not determine this configuration.

SD retains S per-request formulas while expanding request IDs from 240 to 1920. Deterministic per-task scaling changes the complete request-set totals; SD is not exactly eight repetitions of the same S requests. Historical S/SD comparisons are not concurrent density-by-policy interventions.

Regular arrival ignores retained burst-size/spacing options. This synthetic workload does not validate asynchronous RPC, synchronous blocking, shared-data workloads, cross-NUMA routing, persistent gates or production representativeness.
